question: What two main components make up the central nervous system?

options.A: The spinal cord and skin receptors

explanation: The central nervous system strictly consists of the brain and the spinal cord, which act as the main processing center for the body. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T9#BMP111_U1_T9_h1)

question: Why is damage to mature nervous tissue a major concern?

options.A: It has a very limited capacity to heal or regrow
options.B: It stops the production of red blood cells
options.C: It immediately destroys the entire peripheral system

explanation: Nerve cells typically do not divide once fully developed, meaning severe injuries to the brain or spinal cord are often permanent. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T9#BMP111_U1_T9_h1)

question: Which part of the neuron acts as the main receiver of incoming signals from other cells?
explanation: Dendrites branch out widely to catch chemical and electrical messages coming from other nearby neurons. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T9#BMP111_U1_T9_h2)

question: What happens to nerve signals if a disease destroys the myelin sheath around peripheral nerves?

options.A: Neurons multiply to replace the loss
options.B: Signals travel much slower or stop entirely
options.C: Axons disconnect from the cell body permanently
options.D: Signals travel in reverse toward the dendrites

explanation: The myelin sheath acts as an electrical insulator that speeds up impulse conduction; losing it disrupts smooth signal transmission. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T9#BMP111_U1_T9_h2)

question: Which glial cell type forms the myelin sheath around axons in the peripheral nervous system?
explanation: Schwann cells wrap around peripheral nerve fibers to create the protective myelin covering, aiding rapid signal travel outside the brain and spinal cord. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T9#BMP111_U1_T9_h3)

question: What is the main job of microglial cells in the central nervous system?

options.B: Defending against infection and clearing debris
options.C: Transmitting motor commands to skeletal muscles

explanation: Microglia act as immune cells in the brain, clearing away foreign invaders and cellular waste to keep neural tissue healthy. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T9#BMP111_U1_T9_h3)

question: Which ion rushes INTO the neuron when an action potential starts?
explanation: When a neuron is stimulated, sodium channels open and sodium ions flood inward, changing the electrical charge across the membrane. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T9#BMP111_U1_T9_h4)

question: How does myelination affect the speed of a nerve impulse?

options.A: It makes the impulse jump along the axon to increase speed
options.B: It forces the impulse to travel backward
options.C: It slows the impulse down to protect tissue
options.D: It stops the electrical charge from moving

explanation: Myelin acts as insulation so the electrical signal jumps from one gap to the next, moving much faster than in unmyelinated fibers. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T9#BMP111_U1_T9_h4)

question: What name is given to the tiny gap between two communicating neurons?
explanation: The synapse is the functional junction where nerve signals pass from one cell to another via chemical messengers. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T9#BMP111_U1_T9_h5)

question: What is the main role of neurotransmitters in the nervous system?

options.A: To supply physical nourishment and support
options.B: To generate the resting electrical charge
options.C: To carry chemical signals across the synaptic gap
options.D: To insulate the axon and speed up electrical flow

explanation: Because electrical impulses cannot cross the physical gap of a synapse, neurotransmitters bridge the space by carrying the signal chemically. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T9#BMP111_U1_T9_h5)

question: Which type of nervous tissue contains myelinated axons, giving it a whitish appearance?
explanation: White matter gets its name from the fatty myelin sheaths wrapping around the nerve fiber tracts running through it. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T9#BMP111_U1_T9_h6)

question: What is the term for a cluster of nerve cell bodies located outside the central nervous system?
explanation: A ganglion is a collection of neuron cell bodies found in the peripheral nervous system, while similar clusters inside the central nervous system are called nuclei. [learn more](BMP111_U1_T9#BMP111_U1_T9_h6)
